ledger.claim: This is one trip across the three records that matter: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00803, and the trace's first fix (14:00:00) coincides with the trip record's rider_boarded event, so the rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) - that the artifacts describe the same trip - is satisfied before anything else is argued.

I do not overstate the distance point. The policy-computed figures are an optimal route of 2.20 km against a trace of 2.93 km, an excess of 0.73 km - which is 33.18% of the optimal route but falls below the 0.8 km absolute gate - so POL-RD-01 records 'no deviation' and the absolute limb of the establishment test fails. No distance refund is available to the rider on this trip, and on an UPFRONT_QUOTE fare POL-RD-02 would not run even if the gate had passed. The rider's money claim does not depend on the deviation finding; it stands on the fare model instead.

The fare was fixed at booking: fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd of SGD 18.00, so under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges were locked and a detour costs the rider nothing on those lines. What the rider is entitled to is the amount by which charged_total exceeds the quote plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. That is SGD 24.00 charged less SGD 18.00 quoted less SGD 0.00 of properly chargeable pass-throughs = SGD 6.00, refundable in full. The rider's request for the entire SGD 24.00 is not available on an upfront-quoted fare, and I do not press for it; the entitlement is SGD 6.00.

The whole of the over-quote is a single phantom line. The fare breakdown itemises an airport_surcharge of SGD 6.00, but this trip ORIGINATES at Bugis Victoria Street and ends at Suntec City Temasek Boulevard - neither endpoint is Changi or Seletar - so no airport surcharge is chargeable at all. Under POL-RD-09(4) an airport surcharge on a trip that does not originate at an airport is a billing-integrity failure, refunded in full as a standalone correction, and it is available whether or not a deviation exists. The derived properly_chargeable airport surcharge is SGD 0.00. This is a referral for billing integrity under POL-GEN-03, not an escalation, and it does not postpone the money.

Nothing offsets the SGD 6.00. The fare breakdown's derived ERP block shows erp_gantries empty and an erp total of SGD 0.00 (both on-route and off-route), the waiting_time_fee is SGD 0.00, and the airport surcharge is the only non-zero statutory line - so the properly chargeable total is SGD 0.00 and the rider loses nothing from the SGD 6.00 under the pass-through rules of POL-RD-09 and the POL-RD-11(a) computation.

ledger.claim: The driver has no exculpatory clause to stand on here, and I put each of them out of the case: the chat log for TRP-00803 is empty (message_count 0), so no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 can be corroborated or even asserted; the trip record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null and amended_optimal_distance_km null, so no relocation under POL-RD-05 applies; and vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so the pooled-itinerary baseline of POL-RD-12 is not in play. The measured trace stands unadjusted.

The rider's own 60-day counter does not trigger the corroboration requirement in POL-RD-08: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0, well below the threshold of 4, so this claim needs no corroboration beyond the artifacts already cited and is not slowed by that factor. It is cited here only for the test POL-RD-08 names it for.

There is no room for NO_ACTION on the money. The fare breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd of 0.0, so under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION would leave the SGD 6.00 wrongly collected surcharge sitting with the rider. The present state is the rider paying SGD 24.00 for an SGD 18.00 booking, and the evidence does not support that state; the correct outcome for the filing party is a partial refund of SGD 6.00.

No route deviation is established on this trip. Measured the way POL-RD-01 requires — the governing gps_trace polyline of 2.93 km against the booked optimal of 2.2 km — the excess is 0.73 km, which is 33.18% of optimal. POL-RD-01 requires both limbs to pass: an excess greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km in absolute terms. The percentage limb passes; the absolute limb fails, because 0.73 km is below the 0.8 km floor, and the artifact's own derived deviation status reads 'no deviation'. The trace figure and trip_record.actual_distance_km agree at 2.93 km, so there is no conflict between the two distance fields for the driver to answer. On this limb the rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands under POL-GEN-03.

The distance and time elements of this fare are closed to the rider by the pricing model, so the rider's 'journey was longer than needed' ground cannot produce a refund of any size. fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with quoted_fare_sgd 18.00. POL-RD-11 provides that on an upfront-quoted trip the distance and time charges were fixed at booking, POL-RD-02 does not run, and no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess. The rider's percentage figure, whatever it is, is beside the point on an upfront-quoted trip.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and has not discharged it. Limb (b) requires an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. The measured excess is 0.73 km, which fails the 0.8 km absolute limb, so the threshold is not met and the burden never shifts to the driver; the driver is not obliged to point to any exculpatory artifact, and no general assertion about traffic is needed from him. The rider's assertion that the journey 'was longer than needed' attaches no evidence id to any excess figure, and under POL-RD-08 an assertion that cites no evidence id carries no weight.

The trace that governs this case is clean and unimpaired, so no gap-handling and no escalation is in play. EV-GPS-00803 is COMPLETE at weight 1.0: 52 fixes at a 10-second sample interval against an expected 10 seconds, 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and a maximum inter-fix gap of 10 seconds. None of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met — no gap above 90 seconds, no straight-line jump above 500 m, no sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds — so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes, the excess may be read straight off it, and no independent corroboration is required. No POL-RD-10 trigger fires either: the trip identifier TRP-00803 matches across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, the timestamps are consistent and run forwards, no exculpatory clause is invoked against any missing artifact, and no refund above charged_total is in issue.

The 2.2 km booked optimal route stands as the baseline, and it is the absence of a traffic advisory that fixes it there. No traffic advisory covers this trip: EV-ADVIS-00803-01 is MISSING, its admissibility status is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and its weight_multiplier is 0.0 — I disclose that impairment and rely on the absence itself, which is citable. With no advisory on file POL-RD-03 cannot be run and no adjusted optimal route can be computed, so trip_record.optimal_distance_km remains 2.2 km. Nor does POL-RD-05 apply: no pickup or dropoff amendment timestamp appears on the trip_record and amended_optimal_distance_km is null, so there is no re-quote to re-test against, and no substitute figure may be derived. The excess therefore stays at 0.73 km on any adjustment the policy makes available.

The rider's demand for the entire SGD 24.00 has no support in the fare record. The non-surcharge itemisation — base fare 3.80, distance fare 6.00, time fare 7.40 and platform fee 0.80 — sums exactly to the SGD 18.00 quoted at booking, and the billed distance (distance_charged_km 2.93 km) is identical to the trace distance, so no distance or time line is overstated and the driver billed no kilometre he did not drive. The whole of the SGD 6.00 difference is the itemised airport_surcharge line, a pass-through/statutory item that POL-RD-09 settles separately from distance and time. It is not a deviation remedy, it is not a distance or time overcharge, and nothing in it supports a finding about the driver's driving on this trip.

There is no repeat-deviation pattern against this driver, so no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral can arise under POL-RD-06. That test runs on two fields only: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 300, giving a ratio of 0.00 against a trigger of 0.05 and a flag count of 0 against a trigger of 3. Both limbs fail. POL-RD-06 is in any case reached only where POL-RD-01 records a MATERIAL deviation or the evidence is finely balanced, and neither condition holds here. I rely on no other profile field; the lifetime counter prior_deviation_flags is context only and is not the trailing-window figure POL-RD-06 names, as POL-GEN-01 requires.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: part of your claim succeeds. To the driver: the distance allegation fails, but one fare line needs correcting.

The fare. This was an upfront-quoted trip (EV-FARE-00803: fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, quoted_fare_sgd 18.00, total_charged 24.00). The itemised base fare 3.80 + distance fare 6.00 + time fare 7.40 + platform fee 0.80 sum exactly to the 18.00 quote, and the billed distance (distance_charged_km 2.93) equals the trace distance, so no distance or time line is overstated. The whole 6.00 difference is the airport_surcharge line. The trip started at Bugis Victoria Street and ended at Suntec City Temasek Boulevard (EV-TRIP-00803), so it did not originate at Changi or Seletar and no airport surcharge is chargeable. Under POL-RD-09(4) this is a billing-integrity failure and the SGD 6.00 is refunded in full as a standalone correction; POL-RD-11(a) reaches the same figure (SGD 24.00 charged minus SGD 18.00 quoted minus SGD 0.00 of properly chargeable pass-throughs = SGD 6.00). These are the same SGD 6.00, not two payments, and are not added together (POL-RD-11(b)). Nothing offsets it: the derived erp_lines and erp total are SGD 0.00, the waiting_time_fee is SGD 0.00, and the airport surcharge is the only non-zero statutory line (EV-FARE-00803). Your request for the entire SGD 24.00 is refused: on an upfront-quoted fare the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and those lines were properly incurred.

The distance. The governing trace (EV-GPS-00803) measures 2.93 km against a booked optimal of 2.20 km, an excess of 0.73 km — 33.18% of optimal, which passes the percentage limb of POL-RD-01 but fails the 0.8 km absolute limb. No deviation is therefore established, and on an upfront-quoted fare POL-RD-02 would not run in any event (POL-RD-11). On this point the driver's reading is correct: both establishment limbs must pass, and the artifact's own derived status reads 'no deviation'. Both advocates are answered together on this.

No exculpatory clause displaces either conclusion. The chat log for this trip is empty (EV-CHAT-00803: message_count 0), so no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04 can be asserted or corroborated; pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are both null, so POL-RD-05 does not apply and no substitute figure may be derived; vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, so the pooled baseline of POL-RD-12 is not in play. The booked optimal therefore stands at 2.20 km.

The traffic advisory. EV-ADVIS-00803-01 is MISSING, admissibility status MISSING with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0. Because no advisory record covers this trip, POL-RD-03 cannot be run and no external traffic cause carries weight (POL-RD-13). This does not escalate: the missing advisory was not invoked as an exculpatory clause against itself — the driver cites its absence only to fix the baseline — so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged. A separate rider claim about the advisory was discarded by the referee for citing the impaired artifact without naming its issue code, and is not reinstated here.

The trace is unimpaired: 52 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, an empty gaps list and a maximum inter-fix gap of 10 seconds, so none of POL-RD-07(a) to (c) is met and neither POL-RD-07 nor POL-RD-10(3) is in play. Trip identifiers (TRP-00803) match across trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown, and no POL-RD-10 trigger fires.

Repeat-deviation check: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 over completed_trips_90d of 300, so no pattern is established and no POL-RD-06 FULL_REFUND uplift or conduct referral arises. The uncited traffic assertions and the lifetime counters on the profiles are given no weight (POL-GEN-01, POL-RD-08); the mention of prior_deviation_flags is context only and was flagged, not relied on.

Confidence. The deciding facts — the amount charged over the quote (EV-FARE-00803) and the trip's non-airport origin (EV-TRIP-00803) — are carried by artifacts at weight_multiplier 1.0, so confidence is 1.0. The monetary effect of SGD 6.00 does not exceed the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so this ruling executes on issue; execution releases the fare correction under POL-GEN-04's appeal route.

Outcome: PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.00 to the rider, with the billing-integrity referral above; no driver compensation is payable (the billed distance equals the trace distance, so there is no unbilled-distance shortfall under POL-RD-04).

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
referrals: POL-RD-09(4) billing-integrity review: an airport surcharge of SGD 6.00 was applied to trip TRP-00803, which originated at Bugis Victoria Street and ended at Suntec City and therefore did not originate at Changi or Seletar Airport; the line is refunded in full and the fare breakdown should be corrected.
